content: Tobacco use among individuals with mental illness significantly contributes to their reduced life expectancy, which is approximately 25 years shorter than that of the general population. An indirect public health issue associated with cigarette use is the occurrence of accidental fires, which are often linked to alcohol consumption. Various cigarette designs have been proposed, including some by tobacco companies themselves, that would extinguish a cigarette left unattended for more than a minute or two, thereby reducing the risk of fire. However, tobacco companies have historically opposed this concept, arguing that the inconvenience of having to relight a cigarette left untouched for too long would negatively impact their sales. In reality, untreated tobacco formed into a cigarette will naturally extinguish itself relatively quickly if left alone. To counteract this, cigarette tobacco is chemically treated to ensure it smolders continuously and does not extinguish on its own.
